articles.title: Benin don’t plan to mark Lionel Messi as defender reveals they want to give Argentina star the perfect send-off
articles.summary: There could be a cricket score in Buenos Aires tonight with Benin seemingly having no plan to spoil Lionel Messi's party
articles.content:
Benin don’t plan to mark Lionel Messi as defender reveals they want to give Argentina star the perfect send-off

There could be a cricket score in Buenos Aires tonight with Benin seemingly having no plan to spoil Lionel Messi's party

Last Update:

Benin are seemingly ready to party with Lionel Messi on Tuesday night with defender Tijani Mohamed admitting the African side are going to “give everything so that this celebration goes really well”.

Messi will bring the curtain down on his Argentina career in Buenos Aires with a special farewell game in front of an adoring crowd at the Estadio Monumental.

And it appears the adulation also extends to the visitors’ dressing room.

Mohamed told Argentinian TV station C5N: “We don’t need to mark Messi. We are going to enjoy this match. There’s no special plan to defend against Messi, we just have to enjoy this game, and that’s it. I’m going to look at him like this: ‘Messi, you are God’.

“For me he’s the best in the world.”

Benin want to enjoy celebrations with hero Messi

Messi will make his 208th and final appearance for his country and he appears a good bet to increase his goal tally that currently stands at 125 if Mohamed’s approach is anything to go by.

The centre-half, who is currently without a club after his deal at Swiss second division side Yverdon-Sport was terminated last month, says he is totally committed to ensuring his hero gets the send-off he deserves.

He added: “Benin is a very, very good team to play with, but I can’t talk about Benin right now because we have to enjoy this match, and we’re going to give everything so that this celebration goes really well.”

Messi is irreplaceable – Argentina boss Scaloni

It promises to be an emotional night with Argentina boss Lionel Scaloni conceding his side will struggle to replace the eight-time Ballon d’Or winner, considered by many pundits to be the greatest player of all time.

“Leo is irreplaceable,” said Scaloni at Monday’s press conference. “We will seek to continue playing with the same identity, with the idea of being united and playing as a team. It is obvious that without Messi everything changes, but the national team has an identity and the challenge is to continue playing this way, that the guys who come join that cause.”

articles.title: Julian Alvarez makes major agent decision after Arsenal and Barcelona transfer saga
articles.summary: Julian Alvarez is looking to change agents after failing to get a move away from Atletico Madrid in the summer.
articles.content:
Julian Alvarez makes major agent decision after Arsenal and Barcelona transfer saga

Julian Alvarez is looking to change agents after failing to get a move away from Atletico Madrid in the summer.

Last Update:

Julian Alvarez is considering ending his long-standing relationship with agent Fernando Hidalgo.

The Argentina international worked with Hidalgo for almost a decade, but Alvarez and his family are now assessing alternative representation following a turbulent summer surrounding his future.

According to AS, the striker’s inner circle has been searching for a new agency since the transfer window closed, with his father Gustavo Alvarez playing an important role in the process.

An Argentine agency with links to former Paris Saint-Germain midfielder Javier Pastore is reportedly leading the race to represent Alvarez.

Negotiations are said to have reached an advanced stage, although an agreement has not yet been formally signed.

Atletico defended Alvarez after transfer saga

Alvarez was heavily linked with a move away from Atletico, with Barcelona and Arsenal among the clubs associated with the forward.

Despite the speculation, he remained in Madrid after the transfer deadline and is under contract with Atletico until 2030.

The situation created tension around the club, although Atletico’s hierarchy reportedly did not blame Alvarez himself for how events unfolded.

Chief executive Miguel Angel Gil Marin publicly defended the striker at the end of August and suggested attempts had been made to mislead the player during the transfer saga.

A change in the striker’s representation could therefore help ease some of the tension surrounding his future and reset his relationship with Atletico following the events of the summer.

Alvarez focused on Argentina duty

For now, Alvarez is concentrating on his responsibilities with Argentina rather than the uncertainty surrounding his representation.

The forward is away with the national team as they prepare to face Benin in a fixture expected to have added significance because of Lionel Messi’s final appearance.

Messi has been an important influence on Alvarez during his international career, with the pair playing alongside each other during Argentina’s recent period of success.

Alvarez is expected to return to Madrid at the end of the week, when attention will again turn towards his future off the pitch.

articles.title: Why Lamine Yamal was left off 2026 Golden Boy shortlist
articles.summary: Why was Lamine Yamal not nominated for the 2026 Golden Boy shortlist?
articles.content:
Why Lamine Yamal was left off 2026 Golden Boy shortlist

Why was Lamine Yamal not nominated for the 2026 Golden Boy shortlist?

Last Update:

Lamine Yamal is not among the final candidates for the 2026 Golden Boy award despite the Barcelona star remaining one of the most highly-rated young players in world football.

The final shortlist has been revealed after the field was cut down from an initial group of 50 players, with 25 of Europe’s leading Under-21 talents remaining in contention for the prize.

Yamal’s absence immediately stood out given his performances for Barcelona and Spain, but his omission has nothing to do with his form or credentials.

A player cannot win the award more than once and Yamal has already claimed the honour, having been named Golden Boy in 2024.

That previous success means he is automatically ineligible to compete for the award again.

Who is competing for the 2026 Golden Boy award?

The Golden Boy prize was established by Italian newspaper Tuttosport in 2003 and recognises the leading young footballer playing in Europe.

With Yamal unable to win for a second time, several of the continent’s most promising talents are competing to succeed him among the award’s list of winners.

Barcelona are still represented by Pau Cubarsi, Marc Bernal and Xavi Espart, while Real Madrid have Endrick and Yan Diomande among the contenders.

Premier League representation includes Chelsea duo Estevao and Jorrel Hato, Arsenal’s Myles Lewis-Skelly, Brighton pair Charalampos Kostoulas and Luka Vuskovic and Bournemouth’s Junior Kroupi and Rayan.

Manchester City’s Ayoub Bouaddi also features, alongside Bayern Munich’s Lennart Karl, Paris Saint-Germain midfielder Warren Zaire-Emery and Borussia Dortmund duo Joshua Gado and Konstantinos Karetsas.

Rodrigo Mora, Franco Mastantuono, Finn Jeltsch, Kerim Alajbegovic, Said El Mala, Jon Martin, Gianluca Prestianni and Victor Froholdt are also among those competing for the award.

Yamal primed for Ballon d’Or push

Instead, Lamine Yamal will be hoping to get his hands on the coveted Ballon d’Or later this month.

The 19-year-old appears to be facing up against Bayern Munich and England striker Harry Kane for the award.

Polls show the Spaniard neck-and-neck with the former Tottenham man, but Yamal will be keen to become the first Barcelona player to receive the Ballon d’Or since Lionel Messi.

articles.title: Jamie Carragher calls for multi-year Manchester City punishment after guilty charges
articles.summary: Jamie Carragher has had his say on Manchester City's potential punishment from the Premier League.
articles.content:
Jamie Carragher calls for multi-year Manchester City punishment after guilty charges

Jamie Carragher has had his say on Manchester City's potential punishment from the Premier League.

Last Update:

Jamie Carragher believes Manchester City should face sanctions lasting between three and five years if their appeal against the Premier League’s financial verdict is unsuccessful.

An independent commission found City guilty of breaching the league’s financial rules, ruling that they inflated their revenue by more than £830 million across nine seasons between 2009-10 and 2017-18.

No final punishment has been imposed while the appeal process remains ongoing, but Carragher believes a one-season points deduction would not provide a sufficient deterrent if the verdict is upheld.

Speaking on The Overlap Fan Debate, the former Liverpool defender argued that any sanction should instead affect City across multiple campaigns.

“If the people talk about [a penalty of] 80 points or 100 points, but that’s just over one season that gets you relegated and then you come back again,” Carragher said.

“And I think players, a few of them would leave, but I think some of them would say, ‘I could put up with that for a year.’

“But I think, because this has gone on for so long, I do think the punishment should be over a number of years, three to five years, and then players would move on.”

City await outcome of appeal

Carragher’s proposal would potentially have a far greater long-term impact on City’s squad than a punishment confined to a single campaign.

An 80 or 100-point deduction would almost certainly leave a club facing relegation, but Carragher believes City’s resources could allow them to retain much of their squad and quickly return to the Premier League.

A sanction spread across several seasons, he argues, could make it considerably more difficult to convince leading players to remain at the Etihad.

The controversy surrounding City will provide the backdrop to their return to Premier League action against Liverpool at Anfield on Sunday.

The two clubs have been major rivals for domestic honours over recent years and City can expect a difficult reception on Merseyside following the financial verdict.

Former City defender and manager Stuart Pearce believes Enzo Maresca must use the increased hostility as motivation for his players.

“The opposition, they’ll be rolling their sleeves up,” Pearce said. “The atmosphere in the stadiums is going to be red hot. It’s unbelievable it happens to be Liverpool this weekend. It’s going to be electric.

“So it’s going to stimulate everybody else against City, and it’s got to stimulate City against everyone else.”

articles.title: As Lionel Messi stands aside, we ask: Who is the best player in the world right now?
articles.summary: As Lionel Messi departs the international stage, who will stand up and take his crown as the best footballer in the world? We look at the candidates...
articles.content:
As Lionel Messi stands aside, we ask: Who is the best player in the world right now?

As Lionel Messi departs the international stage, who will stand up and take his crown as the best footballer in the world? We look at the candidates...

Last Update:

Lionel Messi plays his final game for Argentina tonight – bringing an end to a magnificent international career and also his eligibility for the title of best player in the world.

Messi was still a contender while appearing on the global stage and his performances in the World Cup over the summer did little to dispel the theory that, even at 39 years of age, he had a legitimate claim.

But his departure from the international game means he will play out his final seasons in Major League Soccer and it would be hard to justify his position as top dog when bullying the opposition for Inter Miami.

Therefore, the stage is cleared for new contenders to assume the mantle of the world’s best. Three of our candidates have been around for some time but with Messi (and to a lesser extent Cristiano Ronaldo, who has been a fading force for a while now) heading into the sunset, they can make their pitches.

There are many players whose numbers defy belief and so there’s an element of personal taste in our selections, as well as the eye-test; which player do you enjoy watching, who gets you off your seat?

Here’s our top five:

5. Kylian Mbappe (Real Madrid)Long talked about as the heir to Messi and Ronaldo, the France striker continues to score goals at an impressive rate at the Santiago Bernabeu and successive Pichichi awards demonstrate his ruthlessness. A career record of 381 goals in 491 club appearances speaks volumes while his strike rate on the international stage – 67 in 107 – is equally formidable.

But there is no denying his move to Madrid has not worked out as planned. Mbappe was brought in to solidify Madrid’s status as the best side in Europe – they won the Champions League two days before his switch to the Spanish capital was confirmed. And yet it has not materialised. Madrid have flopped in the competition since and also fallen behind Barcelona in Spain.

At 27, you could justifiably argue Mbappe’s best days are behind him. His blistering acceleration will start to dwindle while he has already started to sustain niggling injuries that threaten to dilute his influence.

4. Harry Kane (Bayern Munich)Kane has shown Mbappe how to evolve as a footballer while not losing his predatory instincts. Watch Bayern or England and you’re struck by how deep Kane drops, often picking the ball up from the central defenders, to manipulate the game. His range of passing has improved over the years and the way he finds space using an economy of movement is reminiscent of Messi. And then there’s the stats…213 goals in 317 Premier League games for Tottenham and 152 in 154 appearances in all competitions for Bayern.

He’s also England’s record goalscorer and will soon overtake Peter Shilton’s record of 125 appearances.

Kane is 33 years of age but is poised to sign a new deal with Bayern and it’s easy to see why the German champions are eager to tie him down. His game is no longer just about scoring goals, he creates, he leads and he inspires. He has yet to land a major piece of silverware – the Champions League, European Championship or World Cup – but it wouldn’t be a major surprise if that record changed over the next few years.

3. Rodri (Barcelona)The conductor for Spain’s orchestra. The man who makes everything tick for the best international team in the world. Rodri makes football look ridiculously easy. The best defensive midfielder in the game without any doubt, the 30-year-old is one of only two non-forwards to have won the Ballon d’Or in the last 20 years – Luka Modric the other midfield recipient in an era dominated by Messi and Ronaldo.

Rodri has won every major honour, individually and collectively, available in the game. He won the domestic set at Manchester City and both the Euros and World Cup with Spain.

A summer move to Barcelona makes it almost inevitable he will replicate his achievements with City in Spain as well. Strong, physical when necessary but supremely gifted on the ball, Rodri possesses every quality required.

2. Lamine Yamal (Barcelona)What Yamal’s achieved at just 19 years of age is ridiculous. Already a European Championship and World Cup winner, the Barcelona and Spain winger is destined for superstardom for the next decade and beyond. Having made his Barcelona debut at 15, it is easy to forget just how much time he has to improve further, and that is a frightening thought. As a Camp Nou favourite, and also occupying the right-wing role, it is easy to make comparisons with Messi but Yamal’s record at this stage is more impressive. He has already made over 150 appearances for Barca and has three La Liga titles on his CV as well as the 2025 Copa del Rey.

As important as the numbers is the joy he brings, the dancing feet, the drops of the shoulder, the bursts of pace – he passes the eye test with flying colours. He also possesses a swagger, an on-field arrogance that is hard to ignore.

Yamal’s challenge is to maintain this level for the next decade. If he does, he would’ve built a record to challenge Messi’s.

1. Michael Olise (Bayern Munich)This selection may raise a few eyebrows and, admittedly, it does rely more on the eye test than some of the other candidates but when you watch Michael Olise play football, you see greatness in the making. Barca fans will no doubt disagree but he has the highest ceiling of any player on this list. The way he moves, the way he dictates games, the moments of outrageous brilliance that mark him out as a very special footballer. All delivered with a nonchalance, a Gallic shrug that indicates it was nothing out of the ordinary for a man which such natural gifts.

Olise has been special for some time but, this season, he has hit new heights. Twelve goal involvements in seven games for Bayern across domestic and European games highlights his brilliance while his recent appearances for France prove he is playing a different game to most at international level as well. Across Zinedine Zidane’s first four games as France coach, Olise has contributed four goals and two assists. Zidane, arguably one of the greatest players of all time, described him as “exceptional”.

At 24, the world is his to conquer…

articles.title: Lionel Messi’s 10 Greatest Moments For Argentina
articles.summary: As Lionel Messi prepares to play his final game for Argentina, we take a look at his finest moments on the international stage.
articles.content:
Lionel Messi’s 10 Greatest Moments For Argentina

As Lionel Messi prepares to play his final game for Argentina, we take a look at his finest moments on the international stage.

Last Update:

Lionel Messi will bring the curtain down on one of the greatest international careers football has ever seen when he represents Argentina for the final time against Benin on Tuesday.

The 39-year-old is set to make his 208th and final appearance for his country at the Estadio Monumental in Buenos Aires, more than 21 years after his senior debut against Hungary in August 2005.

Messi will bow out as Argentina’s record appearance-maker and goalscorer, having found the net 125 times in 207 games.

His relationship with the national team has not always been straightforward. For years, Messi was judged against Diego Maradona and criticised for failing to reproduce his Barcelona brilliance in an Argentina shirt, with defeats in the 2014 World Cup final and three Copa America finals adding to the pressure.

But the final years of his international career completely transformed that story. Copa America glory finally arrived in 2021 before Messi led Argentina to the World Cup in Qatar 18 months later, while another Copa America triumph followed in 2024.

articles.title: Nations League: Italy go second with Turkey win as Northern Ireland held but remain top
articles.summary: Catch up on all of Monday's action in the Nations League
articles.content:
Nations League: Italy go second with Turkey win as Northern Ireland held but remain top

Catch up on all of Monday's action in the Nations League

Last Update:

A host of nations concluded their international period on Monday with their fourth games in the Nations League.

France completed a dramatic win over Belgium, while Italy took on Turkey, Northern Ireland hosted Georgia and Ukraine faced Hungary.

Check out our rundown of all the results below, while you can check out our in-depth report for the France vs Belgium game using the link above.

Italy 3-1 Turkey

Italy continued their impressive resurgence under Roberto Mancini in the Nations League with a 3-1 victory over Turkey in Bologna.

Gianluca Scamacca opened the scoring before Aral Simsir equalised for the visitors, but Riccardo Calafiori quickly restored Italy’s lead with his first international goal.

Francesco Pio Esposito then added a late third to seal another impressive win for Mancini’s side.

Ukraine 1-2 Hungary

Hungary claimed a crucial 2-1 victory over Ukraine to move level on points with their opponents in Group B2.

Milan Toth put Hungary ahead before Roman Yaremchuk levelled for Ukraine, but Mark Csinger struck five minutes later to restore the visitors’ lead and secure three points.

Northern Ireland 0-0 Georgia

Northern Ireland were held to a goalless draw by Georgia in Belfast despite having the chance to win it from the penalty spot.

Isaac Price saw his late spot-kick saved by Georgia goalkeeper Giorgi Mamardashvili, leaving Northern Ireland still unbeaten but unable to extend their lead at the top of Group B2.

Bosnia and Herzegovina 1-0 Poland

Bosnia and Herzegovina secured a crucial 1-0 victory over Poland thanks to Ivan Basic’s late penalty.

The midfielder struck in the 84th minute to settle a tight contest and move Bosnia onto five points, keeping them firmly in the Group B4 promotion race.

Romania 0-1 Sweden

Sweden maintained their unbeaten start with a narrow victory over Romania in Bucharest.

Viktor Gyokeres scored the only goal after 12 minutes, giving Sweden another important three points at the top end of Group B4.

Cyprus 2-1 Latvia

Cyprus came from behind to beat Latvia 2-1 in Group C2. Eduards Daskevics put Latvia ahead after the break, but Ioannis Pittas equalised before Marcus Edwards scored in stoppage time to complete the comeback.

Montenegro 0-0 Armenia

Montenegro were held to a goalless draw by Armenia, missing the chance to strengthen their position at the top of Group C2. Armenia defended resolutely to claim a valuable point away from home.

articles.title: Tottenham handed Micky van de Ven injury boost ahead of Manchester United clash
articles.summary: Micky van de Ven's injury he picked up on international duty is not believed to be too serious.
articles.content:
Tottenham handed Micky van de Ven injury boost ahead of Manchester United clash

Micky van de Ven's injury he picked up on international duty is not believed to be too serious.

Last Update:

Tottenham have been handed a positive update on Micky van de Ven after the defender was forced off during the Netherlands’ 2-1 Nations League win over Serbia.

Van de Ven suffered a hand injury after Serbia striker Luka Jovic landed on him during Sunday’s match and was unable to continue.

The sight of the Spurs captain leaving the pitch provided another potential injury concern for Roberto De Zerbi ahead of the return of Premier League football.

However, Netherlands head coach Xavi played down the severity of the problem after the match, describing it as “not a big problem.”

Spurs travel to Old Trafford looking for their first Premier League win of the season after a difficult opening five matches.

King backs Van de Ven as Tottenham captain

Former Tottenham captain Ledley King believes Van de Ven has developed into the right player to lead the club.

King praised the Netherlands international’s individual qualities but believes the next stage of his development will involve raising the standards of those around him.

“I think he’s a fantastic player. His new role now is to make the players around him better,” King said.

“I think Micky takes care of himself. His ability to recover and put fires out is something we’ve seen over the last few years. That’s an important element for the team.

“So, I think the next role is to manage the group and get the best out of the group as a team.

“He’s grown into the role. Having seen Micky on the pitch, he leads by example, for sure and I think he was the right choice to be captain.”

articles.title: Thomas Tuchel hails King Kane as he prepares to equal England appearance record
articles.summary: Harry Kane will match Peter Shilton's England appearance record when he leads out the Three Lions against Czechia on Tuesday night
articles.content:
Thomas Tuchel hails King Kane as he prepares to equal England appearance record

Harry Kane will match Peter Shilton's England appearance record when he leads out the Three Lions against Czechia on Tuesday night

Last Update:

Thomas Tuchel believes Harry Kane’s move to Bayern Munich has taken him to a new level with the England captain set to match a long-standing Three Lions record against Czechia on Tuesday night.

Kane comes into the Nations League clash one short of Peter Shilton’s all-time appearance record of 125 and will equal the former Southampton and Nottingham Forest goalkeeper’s mark when he leads England out at Wembley.

The 33-year-old, who netted twice in Saturday’s 7-0 hammering of Croatia to increase his England record tally to 89, joined Bayern from Tottenham in 2023 and has helped the club to two Bundesliga titles and one DFB-Pokal.

Former Bayern boss Tuchel said: ”I’m not sure I have anymore words [for Kane].

“He’s on the shortlist for the Ballon d’Or. We’ve spoken so often about him and I try to find new words which then make no sense!

“Everything he does, he does it on the highest level, he does it consecutively and I am very sure he will be the one leading the team out onto the training pitch, he will lead the team in the warm-up and not do one step less or one step slower. That is the level he has.

“Since he took this major role for Bayern Munich, he found a new level. It’s the highest level, on and off the pitch.”

England star Kane a goalscoring machine

Kane’s numbers continue to mark him out as one of the best number nines of his generation.

He is second on the all-time Premier League goalscoring list with 213 and has hit another 152 in just 154 games in all competitions for Bayern.

“All these number nines in world football, no matter in which league, they are built a bit different,” added Tuchel.

“They don’t only do it so their team wins, they also do it for themselves and for the records, ‘how many can I score? How many can I assist? Where is the next record?’

“That’s what drives them and it’s good that drives them. You will not find a striker of this calibre who does not have these individual goals.”

England suffer injury blows with Scott and Konsa ruled out

It wasn’t all good news for Tuchel on Monday, though, with Bournemouth midfielder Alex Scott and Arsenal defender Ezri Konsa having to return to their clubs due to injury.

Konsa’s is not thought to be serious but Scott could be facing up to two months on the sidelines with a quad issue.

“With Alex, it’s a strange one, I’m very sad about it,” said Tuchel. “He trained in full before Croatia, did extra work after the training sessions, we knew he was in treatment but there were only green lights from him and the medics.

“When we were aware there was slight discomfort during the match and asked if he wanted to come off he said no. After the match, he said he could have played 90 minutes and didn’t feel an injury.

“Even before the scan he didn’t feel injured so it’s a strange one. There was zero risk taken from our side.”

Bournemouth unhappy at Scott injury

Bournemouth are thought to be unhappy with England’s treatment of Scott and Tuchel has sympathy with the Premier League strugglers.

“On a human level, I feel bad that he does not get his next cap tomorrow,” he said. “In my mind, he [would have] started tomorrow.

“I would not have taken any risk, even if it was a big opportunity for him. We wanted him to start but if we had the slightest idea it was a risk [to play him], we would not have taken it. We never do this. We – the medical and physical department – are always in communication with all the players who are with us.

“We share information, this is a totally open process. I can understand that Bournemouth are not happy because they lose a key player. But I can just say that from the moment we took the decision there was absolutely no risk apparent to me or our physical staff. It’s a one off.”

On Konsa, Tuchel added: “Ezri felt discomfort when he came into camp, played with it against Spain and it got a bit worse so he stayed in camp and tried everything for the match against Czechia and it came too soon.

“He tried everything for the game in Croatia, got the green light and came through all the training sessions so was ready to play.

“Unfortunately, he got another hit on the quad and that caused a light trauma and we decided not to let him play through this pain, so he left camp to get treatment for both his issues now. I think nothing major but not worth the risk taking.

articles.title: Manchester City star Haaland not injured but fatigued as he jets away for mini-break
articles.summary: Erling Haaland will recharge his batteries with a mini-break before returning to the chaos surrounding Manchester City
articles.content:
Manchester City star Haaland not injured but fatigued as he jets away for mini-break

Erling Haaland will recharge his batteries with a mini-break before returning to the chaos surrounding Manchester City

Last Update:

Norway coach Stale Solbakken defended Erling Haaland and several other Premier League players after they hired a private jet and made a swift getaway from Porto last night.

Just half an hour after the final whistle sounded at the Estadio do Dragao following Norway’s 2-1 defeat to Portugal, Haaland, Martin Odegaard, Sander Berge and Kristoffer Ajer were spotted getting into a minibus and being whisked to a local airport to travel back to England.

It is believed from there they will disappear for a short holiday before the Premier League resumes this weekend.

Solbakken told VG: “It wasn’t just Haaland who left early. There’s a whole bunch of people leaving now. They need a breather. They have been given a few days off from their clubs.

“I understand that they book a private plane when they have two or three days off. You have to remember that the teams that went far in the World Cup have many players who have had minimal holiday time. Then it’s right into the start of the season and then a mini international tournament. It’s an extreme strain.”

Haaland went off due to exhaustion

Haaland lasted 67 minutes of the game against Portugal before signalling to come off. He was spotted with a slight limp when leaving the stadium but Solbakken said the substation was always pre planned.

He added: “We were hoping for 60 minutes after the conversation we had yesterday, and he managed just over 65.”

When he returns from his mini-holiday, Haaland will walk into the maelstrom that has been absorbing Manchester City while he has been away.

City were found guilty on 114 charges of financial malpractice and also of obfuscating the investigation. They have denied any wrongdoing and last week appealed the verdict.

Former Borussia Dortmund star Haaland has not spoken on the subject since linking up with Norway and the City players are likely to be kept away from the media ahead of Sunday’s game at Liverpool.

City can expect a hostile reception at Anfield with Liverpool the club that have arguably suffered more than any other as a result of City’s methods.

articles.title: Alex Scott facing two-month absence after withdrawing from England squad
articles.summary: Alex Scott is facing a spell on the sidelines due to a quad injury in what will be a bitter blow for Bournemouth
articles.content:
Alex Scott facing two-month absence after withdrawing from England squad

Alex Scott is facing a spell on the sidelines due to a quad injury in what will be a bitter blow for Bournemouth

Last Update:

Alex Scott has withdrawn from the England squad and could miss the next two months with a quad injury.

The Bournemouth midfielder sustained the injury during his first international start against Croatia on Saturday, playing 70 minutes before being replaced by Everton’s James Garner.

The 23-year-old will undergo further tests when he returns to the South Coast club but The Athletic are reporting he could be absent for up to eight weeks in what will be a bitter blow to Cherries boss Marco Rose.

He has already been ruled out of Tuesday night’s game with Czechia at Wembley.

Scott stars for Bournemouth

Scott has been a key player for Bournemouth this season, starting all five games, scoring once and adding an assist.

He also made a huge impression with England, looking very comfortable alongside Elliot Anderson and Jude Bellingham in a midfield three that was instrumental in the Three Lions cruising to a 7-0 win in Rijeka.

Scott has grown in prominence since joining Bournemouth in 2023 from Bristol City and is now widely regarded as one of the best young midfielders in the country.

Rose’s side have yet to win in the Premier League this season, recording three draws and two defeats. They visit Chelsea when the league resumes this weekend before home games against Sturm Graz, in the Europa League, and Sunderland.

articles.title: Portuguese chief confident he can solve ‘misunderstanding’ but Jesus won’t apologise to Ronaldo
articles.summary: FPF president Pedro Proenca is confident he can broker peace between Jorge Jesus and Cristiano Ronaldo  and that the five-time Ballon d'Or winner will return to the squad in November
articles.content:
Portuguese chief confident he can solve ‘misunderstanding’ but Jesus won’t apologise to Ronaldo

FPF president Pedro Proenca is confident he can broker peace between Jorge Jesus and Cristiano Ronaldo  and that the five-time Ballon d'Or winner will return to the squad in November

Last Update:

Portuguese Football Federation (FPF) president Pedro Proenca is confident the “misunderstanding” between Jorge Jesus and Cristiano Ronaldo will be resolved and hopes the veteran striker will return to the squad in November.

Ronaldo walked out on the team prior to last week’s Nations League game in Denmark following a row with Jesus that stemmed from the coach’s decision not to bring him off the bench against Norway the previous weekend.

The 41-year-old flew back from Copenhagen in his private jet just hours before the Denmark game and was not considered for last night’s return against the Norwegians in Porto, a game the hosts won 2-1 with Ronaldo’s replacement Goncalo Ramos scoring the deciding goal 11 minutes from time.

Ronaldo will return to action for club side Al-Nassr this Friday and it is hoped a resolution can be found prior to the November international break.

Proenca told RTP: “The FPF is not a house without rules but these dynamics happen within a working group.

“There is a very strong relationship between Jorge Jesus and Cristiano Ronaldo. If that were not the case, maybe Ronaldo would have already retired from the national team. Everything that will happen in the next few days are moments of tranquility, conversation, discussion and what we want is that in November he can be with our squad again.”

Ronaldo is our legend – Proenca

Proenca needs to tread a tricky line in not undermining Jesus but also attempting to smooth the waters for Ronaldo’s return.

“Ronaldo is the best player of all time,” added Proenca. “He has given more than two decades to Portuguese football. Cristiano Ronaldo is the greatest symbol of Portugueseness. He is in the national team for his own sporting merit and this is absolutely unquestionable. He will always be part of this squad whenever he is technically capable. Cristiano knows that this is the feeling.

“On the specific subject, let me say that we are facing a misunderstanding that has to be resolved internally. He’s part of the squad, he’s our legend. He was the captain for the first of these four games. The coach says he counts on him.

“Cristiano Ronaldo is a Portuguese legend, an absolutely extraordinary player who could have ended his career after the World Cup but did not want to do it because of the love he has for his national team. I am a witness of this relationship that Cristiano has with the Portuguese people, with our team. Therefore, now that these four games are over, we will all have time and tranquility to sit down and solve a misunderstanding.

“Ronaldo is part of our heritage and will be here whenever the coach wants him to be.”

Jesus – I won’t apologise to Ronaldo

Jesus said he would be happy to see Ronaldo return but ruled out apologising for not bringing the former Real Madrid superstar off the bench.

“I don’t apologise to anyone,” he said. “The problem that started all of this was that the player was warming up. I made the decision [not to bring him on]. What do I have to apologise for?”

He added: “I don’t know what Cris will decide. I’ve already said what I have to say, but I’ll add, for me, at first it was never a situation. It was something I thought was normal as a coach. There are principles as a coach that are non-negotiable.

“For me Cris will be in the next squad if he is playing for Al-Nassr and he wants to return to the national team. You can’t change, in my opinion, a one-year friendship in a situation that you can’t understand. It was something he created himself, and maybe well because he’s a legend, this whole problem of coming on, warming up, not coming on… How many warmed up today and didn’t come on? Will there be any problem? No. With Cris it’s different, he’s a legend. But is it a problem? It’s not a problem for me. If Cris wants to and is playing for Al-Nassr he will be called up. But it’s Cris who will decide.”

Portugal’s next games are during the November international break when they host Denmark before taking on Wales in Cardiff.

articles.title: Nations League: Wales lose again as Netherlands go top of group
articles.summary: Catch up on Sunday's Nations League fixtures
articles.content:
Nations League: Wales lose again as Netherlands go top of group

Catch up on Sunday's Nations League fixtures

Last Update:

Another packed night of Nations League action saw Wales take on Denmark and Netherlands face Serbia in the Nations League Division A.

Check out our round-up of all the action from Sunday, while you can also find in-depth reports for Portugal vs Norway, Greece vs Germany and Republic of Ireland vs Israel.

Wales 0-1 Denmark

Wales suffered a narrow 1-0 defeat to Denmark in Cardiff, with Rasmus Hojlund scoring the only goal from the penalty spot.

Danny Ward had produced several important saves but was punished in the 73rd minute after miskicking a pass and colliding with Gustav Isaksen, allowing Højlund to convert from 12 yards.

Craig Bellamy’s side pushed for an equaliser but could not find a way through as Denmark secured another important three points, with Wales suffering their third defeat in four Nations League games to leave them in danger of relegation from Division A.

Netherlands 2-1 Serbia

The Netherlands moved top of Group A2 after edging Serbia 2-1 at the Philips Stadion. Virgil van Dijk opened the scoring on his 100th international appearance, only for Mihajlo Cvetkovic to quickly restore parity for the visitors.

Joshua Zirkzee then pounced in the second half to grab the winner and maintain the Dutch unbeaten run under new manager Xavi Hernandez.

Kosovo 1-1 Austria

Kosovo and Austria shared the points in a 1-1 draw in Group B3. The result means Austria remain unbeaten after four matches, having previously beaten Israel and Kosovo before drawing with Ireland.

Kosovo, meanwhile, claimed a useful point after defeats against Austria and Ireland.

Malta 1-0 Andorra

Malta claimed another victory in League D with a 1-0 win over Andorra. The result keeps Malta firmly in contention at the top of Group D1 after their earlier victory over Andorra and draws against Gibraltar.

Azerbaijan 1-0 Lithuania

Azerbaijan edged Lithuania 1-0 to claim their first win of the Nations League campaign. After draws against Lithuania and Liechtenstein in their opening two matches, the victory gives Azerbaijan a major boost in Group D2.
